newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser to hold pulp prices for now.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser to hold pulp prices for now.

text.p: Weyerhaeuser Co has no plans to raise pulp prices next month but may seek to boost prices $50 a ton later in the year if market conditions improve, a company spokeswoman said Wednesday.
Montye Male confirmed that president and chief executive officer Jack Creighton told analysts the company will not try to implement a price hike next month.
Male said Creighton indicated the company was likely to boost prices by $50 a ton as market conditions improved, and she said he was optimistic about the second half of the year.
Northern bleached softwood kraft, a benchmark grade, currently carries a list price of about $580 a ton, analyst Steven Dietrich of Jensen Securities said.
Pulp and linerboard prices have eroded in recent weeks, hurting paper company earnings in a trend likely to spill over into the current quarter, Dietrich said.
But inventories should tighten later in the year as Weyerhaeuser and other companies reduce production, he said.
Dietrich cut his estimate for Weyerhaeuser's 1997 earnings to $2.40 a share from $2.70, compared with $2.34 in 1996. He left unchanged his 1998 estimate of $3.20 a share.
